title: An AI-supervised remote exam went so badly that 58,000 students must retake it
gist: UNAM's first fully remote entrance exam for ~160,000 applicants, secured by Respondus LockDown Browser plus Territorium AI webcam proctoring, produced a 4.7x jump in top scores (16.3% scoring 100+ vs a 3.5% 2021-25 baseline), and an expert commission is forcing roughly 58,000 people — including admits going back to 2021 — to re-sit in person. It is a live demonstration that current AI-proctoring stacks fail against consumer LLMs and off-camera assistance at scale.

insights.claim: On UNAM's 2026 remote entrance exam, 16.3 percent of test takers scored 100 or more out of 120 questions, versus a 3.5 percent average over 2021-2025 — a roughly 4.7x jump in the top-score rate.
insights.speaker: Nate Anderson
insights.so_what: Score-distribution drift is the cheapest available integrity audit for any remote assessment; institutions and testing vendors without this baseline monitoring are flying blind.

insights.claim: The distortion was most extreme in the extreme tail: 5.5 percent of applicants scored 110 or more this year against a 0.9 percent 2021-2025 baseline, a roughly 6x increase.
insights.speaker: Nate Anderson
insights.so_what: Cheating aids compress the top of the distribution, so tail-percentile drift is a more sensitive detector than mean drift — a design principle for any integrity monitoring product.
insights.locator: The story was even worse at the highest of the high end

insights.claim: An AI expert told NPR that statistical modeling suggested almost half of the students were cheating on the online exam, implying misconduct was the norm rather than the exception.
insights.speaker: Nate Anderson
insights.so_what: If ~50% cheating rates are achievable against a commercial lockdown-browser-plus-AI-proctoring stack, the entire remote high-stakes testing category has a credibility problem, not a tuning problem.
insights.quote: that almost half of the students were cheating when taking the exam online
insights.locator: AI expert Raul Rojas, speaking to NPR

insights.claim: UNAM canceled nearly 2 percent of total exams for conduct issues while its own analysis concedes a significant number of applicants may have received help — a detection rate roughly an order of magnitude below the estimated cheating rate.
insights.speaker: Nate Anderson
insights.so_what: The gap between 2% caught and ~50% estimated is the quantified failure rate of the proctoring stack, and the number any competing vendor will have to beat.
insights.quote: the probability that a significant number of applicants may have received help
insights.locator: These measures do not seem to have worked well

themes.theme: Proctoring tech stack and its failure modes

insights.claim: UNAM's remote exam used the Respondus LockDown Browser, which blocks printing, copying, other web addresses, other applications, web searches, instant messaging and browser minimizing for the duration of the test.
insights.speaker: Nate Anderson
insights.so_what: Named vendor exposure: Respondus is now attached to the largest publicly documented remote-exam failure to date, which is reputational risk in every enterprise and university procurement it enters.
insights.quote: unable to print, copy, go to other web addresses, or access other applications on the computer
insights.locator: Because this year’s exam was administered remotely

insights.claim: UNAM layered a Territorium AI webcam proctoring system on top of the lockdown browser to detect person-substitution, cell phones, earphones, and applicants leaving the camera frame.
insights.speaker: Nate Anderson
insights.so_what: This is a defense-in-depth configuration that still failed, which argues the problem is architectural rather than a matter of adding another detection layer.
insights.locator: UNAM also used a proctoring system from Territorium

insights.claim: The human oversight layer ran at one supervisor per 150 applicants, with supervisors acting only on alerts generated by the AI system rather than watching independently.
insights.speaker: Nate Anderson
insights.so_what: A 1:150 alert-triage ratio means human review can only be as good as the model's recall; staffing economics, not model quality, may be the binding constraint on remote proctoring.
insights.locator: The test also had one human supervisor for every 150 applicants

insights.claim: The cheating techniques circulating before the exam were physical workarounds to the camera's field of view — placing a second monitor running ChatGPT outside the frame, hiding earphones under hair, or having a proxy test-taker sit off camera.
insights.speaker: Nate Anderson
insights.so_what: Software lockdown secures the device but not the room; any proctoring product that reasons only about the machine and one camera cone is structurally defeatable and should be priced accordingly.
insights.quote: Online accounts advised students to position monitors outside the web-camera frame where they could access ChatGPT or other AI models.
insights.locator: A New York Times report last week

insights.claim: Because the exam was multiple choice rather than essay-based, the usual forensic signatures of AI cheating such as complete answers pasted instantly into text boxes are unavailable, making post-hoc attribution nearly impossible.
insights.speaker: Nate Anderson
insights.so_what: Assessment format determines auditability: multiple-choice formats that once resisted plagiarism now resist detection instead, which may push high-stakes testing back toward written and in-person formats.
insights.locator: No one yet knows what kinds of cheating may have taken place

themes.theme: Institutional cost of an integrity failure

insights.claim: The remediation extends far beyond the compromised cohort: the control exam applies to everyone admitted on minimum program scores since 2021, putting roughly 58,000 people's existing places at UNAM back in play.
insights.speaker: Nate Anderson
insights.so_what: A single remote-exam failure retroactively contaminated five prior admission cycles — the liability tail of assessment-integrity failure is far longer than the incident itself.
insights.locator: This control exam will apply not only to those

insights.claim: UNAM must run the in-person control exam against a hard deadline, with classes scheduled to begin August 10 and no delay yet announced.
insights.speaker: Nate Anderson
insights.so_what: Compressed remediation timelines mean emergency procurement of in-person testing capacity and proctors, a demand spike that favors legacy physical testing providers over remote-proctoring vendors.
insights.locator: Details on the control exam should appear soon

insights.claim: UNAM's rector apologized to honest applicants but defended the retest as necessary to guarantee equity in access, showing institutions will impose collective costs on innocent participants rather than accept a tainted admissions cycle.
insights.speaker: Nate Anderson
insights.so_what: Institutional preference for credential credibility over individual fairness sets the expected response template for the next AI-cheating scandal at scale.
insights.quote: necessary to give certainty and guarantee equity in access

insights.claim: The expert commission's recommended remedy was not better technology but reversion to a proctored physical exam room with a human supervisor.
insights.speaker: Nate Anderson
insights.so_what: The most credible institution in Mexican higher education just concluded that AI proctoring is not fixable in the near term — a bearish read-through for the remote-proctoring software category and bullish for physical test-center operators.
insights.quote: Now, almost 58,000 applicants will have to try again in an official exam room, watched by a human proctor.

insights.claim: Nearly 160,000 applicants sat the exam remotely over several weeks from late May through early June, meaning the test window itself was long enough for cheating techniques to be shared and refined between sittings.
insights.speaker: Nate Anderson
insights.so_what: Multi-week testing windows convert individual exploits into distributed public knowledge; window length is an underrated integrity variable in remote assessment design.
